summary: This file implements a code snippet viewer component with optional AI-powered line-by-line explanations and summaries. It handles syntax highlighting via Prism, maps programming languages to icons and styling variants, and provides both a collapsible code block and an expandable explanation feature. The component intelligently detects the language from filenames, props, or React children, and can display detailed annotations for specific lines when available.

explanations.14: useTokenize is a hook from prism-react-renderer that breaks code into tokens while respecting line boundaries — this prevents the problem of multi-line comments/strings getting split across HTML tags when you naively split highlighted code by newlines.
explanations.57: React.isValidElement checks if something is actually a React component or element (as opposed to a plain string or number), so we know it's safe to access its .props.
explanations.63: match() returns an array like ['language-javascript', 'javascript'] if the regex finds a hit, or null if not — accessing match[1] gets just the language name part.
explanations.68: We need to check if nested is an array because props.children can be either a single React node or an array of them depending on how many child elements there are.
explanations.145: This TypeScript interface is a blueprint describing what shape each language icon entry should have — iconClassName is a CSS class string, iconify is an icon library identifier, and ariaLabel is accessibility text.
explanations.337: We store the timeout ID in useRef so we can cancel it later if needed (e.g., if the component unmounts before the 1-second timer finishes).
explanations.359: badgeRefs is a lookup table storing button references keyed by line number — this lets us find where each '?' badge is positioned so we can place the tooltip above it.
explanations.377: useMemo caches the grammar lookup result and only recomputes it when lang changes, avoiding unnecessary Prism.languages lookups on every render.
explanations.386: After Prism tokenizes, if the code ends with a newline, useTokenize adds a synthetic empty final 'line' — we strip it so line numbers stay 1-based and match the eli5 object keys.
explanations.395: getBoundingClientRect() returns the badge button's pixel position on screen; we use its coordinates to calculate where the fixed-position tooltip should appear.
explanations.406: This toggles the active line: if you click the same badge twice, it closes; clicking a different badge opens that one instead.
explanations.417: We listen for scroll and resize events so that if the user scrolls the page or resizes the window while a tooltip is open, it stays glued to its badge instead of drifting away.
explanations.425: This just grabs the explanation text for whichever line is currently active, or null if none is active.
explanations.449: lineNum is the 1-based line number (i + 1) converted to a string because the eli5 object keys are strings like '1', '2', '3'.
explanations.466: This callback ref pattern stores each badge button in the badgeRefs lookup table keyed by its line number, so positionTooltip() can find it later.
explanations.532: useId() generates a unique ID, and we prefix it to create a content ID — this associates the toggle button's aria-controls attribute with the summary div's id for accessibility.
explanations.536: When open is true, we set maxHeight to the div's full scrollHeight (how tall it wants to be), triggering a CSS transition to that height; when false, we collapse it back to 0px.
explanations.603: We parse the injected JSON string (which came from a .eli5.json sidecar file) into a JavaScript object; if it's malformed, we catch the error and return null so the feature just degrades gracefully.
explanations.615: We check if eli5summary exists, is a string, and has non-whitespace content — if so, trim it; otherwise set it to null so the Show/Hide block won't render.
explanations.627: We try detecting the language in priority order: first from the pluginLang prop, then by looking for class names in the children, then by parsing the filename extension, falling back to plaintext.
explanations.649: resolve is a function that swaps out %%variableName%% markers with user-provided values, enabling personalized snippets — we get it from a React context.
explanations.664: We choose which code block renderer to use: if we have both code text and line-by-line annotations, use the fancy Eli5CodeBlock; if just code, use the standard Docusaurus CodeBlock; otherwise render whatever children were passed in.
explanations.682: We check if the filename indicates a Docker-related file by testing various naming patterns — this determines whether to show the Docker icon even if the lang property didn't say 'docker'.
explanations.698: variantKey determines which CSS class and icon set to use; it's either the explicit variant prop, auto-detected from special cases like Docker/Docusaurus, or looked up from the language, defaulting to 'none'.
explanations.754: The summary block only renders if the snippet is already open (otherwise it looks like a second accordion header below the closed code block) and if eli5Summary actually exists.
